content: ABO incompatibility occurs when the immune system reacts to the mixing of two incompatible blood types. This reaction can lead to serious complications, particularly during blood transfusions or organ transplants. Symptoms of ABO Incompatibility The symptoms of a transfusion reaction due to ABO incompatibility include: Back pain Blood in the urine A sensation of impending doom Fever Yellowing of the skin (jaundice) Causes of ABO Incompatibility The ABO blood group system is based on the presence or absence of specific molecules (antigens) on the surface of red blood cells. These antigens are classified into three major blood types: A, B, and O. Blood type A has A antigens (AA or AO molecules). Blood type B has B antigens (BB or BO molecules). Blood type AB has both A and B antigens. Blood type O lacks any antigens. Individuals with one blood type produce antibodies against the antigens of other blood types. For example: A person with type A blood will form antibodies against type B and type AB blood. A person with type B blood will form antibodies against type A and type AB blood. A person with type O blood will form antibodies against type A, type B, and type AB blood. Type O blood, which lacks surface antigens, does not trigger an immune response in recipients of other blood types. This makes type O individuals universal donors. However, people with type O blood can only receive type O blood due to their antibodies. Both blood and plasma transfusions must be carefully matched to avoid immune reactions, as antibodies are present in the plasma. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care If you have recently undergone a blood transfusion or organ transplant and experience any of the symptoms listed above, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Diagnosis The diagnosis of ABO incompatibility may involve: Elevated bilirubin levels. A complete blood count (CBC) showing damaged red blood cells and possibly mild anemia. Laboratory testing of both the patient’s and donor’s blood to confirm incompatibility. Treatment Options Treatment for ABO incompatibility may include: Antihistamines to manage allergic reactions. Steroids to reduce swelling and allergic responses. Intravenous fluids to maintain hydration and support circulation. Medications to stabilize blood pressure if it drops too low. Prevention Careful testing of both donor and recipient blood types before transfusion or transplantation is essential to prevent ABO incompatibility reactions. Prognosis ABO incompatibility can be a life-threatening condition. However, with prompt and appropriate treatment, full recovery is likely.
